study_identification_part.si_4_title: Heterogeneous brain dynamic functional connectivity patterns in first-episode drug-naive patients with major depressive disorder

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: The study utilized data from the International Big-Data Center for Depression Research (IBCDR). Specifically, it included a matched cohort of 91 first-episode drug-naive (FEDN) MDD patients and 91 healthy controls from a single center, as well as an independent sample of 125 controls from two other centers used as a 'healthy-ICA group'.

Another independent sample (125 control individuals, 71 females) from the other two centers... was a healthy-ICA group

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: The 91 healthy-base controls were used to build second-order polynomial regression normative models for 40 brain features using 10-fold cross-validation. The 91 FEDN-MDD patients were evaluated against these models to calculate individual deviations (z-scores), which were then used for subtype clustering. The 125 controls in the healthy-ICA group were used to estimate group-level independent components (ICs) for GIG-ICA guidance.

dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: The normative modeling approach involved 40 separate second-order polynomial regression models (one for each of the 20 IC measures and 20 fluctuation coefficients), all derived from the same 'healthy-base group' of 91 individuals. Training was conducted via 10-fold cross-validation, but the specific training set size per fold was not explicitly reported (though implicitly ~82).
